sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy and Utilities anchor the market as the only "all-green" sectors, while Financials and Consumer Defensive lose momentum and slip in the rankings.

Energy and Utilities are currently driving market strength, standing out as the only two sectors out of 11 to achieve "all-green" status across all timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, and YTD). Energy remains the dominant leader with a momentum score of 0.933 (YTD rank 1), while Utilities climbed +2 spots to rank 5 with a momentum score of 0.600. Basic Materials also showed upward mobility, gaining +2 spots to reach rank 6 with a momentum score of 0.417.

Conversely, defensive and financial sectors are rotating downward. Consumer Defensive and Financials were the week's biggest losers, both dropping -2 spots to ranks 7 and 8, respectively. Meanwhile, Consumer Cyclical (momentum 0.083, rank 11) and Communication Services (momentum 0.133, rank 10) remain pinned to the bottom of the momentum table.

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth**: Only 2 of 11 sectors—Energy (momentum 0.933) and Utilities (momentum 0.600)—are "all-green," showing positive performance across the week, month, quarter, half-year, and YTD.
* **Energy's Top Spot**: Energy maintains its absolute lead in the market, holding the #1 YTD rank with a dominant momentum score of 0.933.
* **Technology Resiliency**: Technology remains a key pillar of strength, securing the #2 YTD rank with a robust momentum score of 0.817.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers**: Basic Materials (rank 6, momentum 0.417) and Utilities (rank 5, momentum 0.600) both improved their standings by +2 spots over the last five sessions.
* **Top Losers**: Consumer Defensive (rank 7, momentum 0.283) and Financials (rank 8, momentum 0.550) experienced the sharpest declines, each dropping -2 spots.
* **Deep Laggards**: Consumer Cyclical (momentum 0.083) and Communication Services (momentum 0.133) continue to lag significantly, ranking 11th and 10th YTD respectively.

## Divergences
* **Healthcare Undercurrents**: Healthcare exhibits a strong momentum score of 0.600, diverging positively from its low YTD rank of 9.
* **Industrials Softening**: Industrials holds a high YTD rank of 3, yet its momentum score has cooled to 0.517, placing it among the momentum laggards.
* **No Fragile All-Green Signals**: No sectors are currently flagged with fragile all-green divergences, indicating that the positive trends in Energy and Utilities remain structurally supported.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy, railroads, and healthcare REITs anchor a defensive market leadership, while a sharp rotation hits Internet Content and Airlines as commodities like Silver and Uranium begin to emerge.

The US industry landscape on 2026-07-23 reveals a highly concentrated leadership profile, with only 20 of 144 groups maintaining "all-green" status across all timeframes. Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.95) and Railroads (momentum 0.88) anchor this top tier, displaying sustained strength alongside REIT - Healthcare Facilities (momentum 0.88).

Meanwhile, rapid rotations are underway. Capital is flowing into defensive and commodity groups, with Silver (+23 spots) and Utilities - Renewable (+16 spots) posting major weekly gains. Conversely, growth and travel sectors are fading rapidly; Internet Content & Information collapsed 32 spots to rank 95, and Airlines fell 20 spots to rank 88.

## Strength
* **Narrow Breadth:** Just 13.9% of the market (20 of 144 groups) is in an all-green posture, led by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing, Railroads, and REIT - Healthcare Facilities.
* **Momentum Leaders:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing holds the top momentum score of 0.950 (YTD rank 3), followed closely by Railroads at 0.883 and REIT - Healthcare Facilities at 0.882.
* **Sustained Performance:** Oil & Gas Midstream, Textile Manufacturing, and Consumer Electronics join the top momentum leaders as the market's most resilient industries across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Silver surged 23 spots to rank 72 (momentum 0.51), while Conglomerates (+17 spots to rank 60, momentum 0.68) and Utilities - Renewable (+16 spots to rank 50, momentum 0.53) showed strong weekly acceleration.
* **Top Losers:** Internet Content & Information plunged 32 spots to rank 95 (momentum 0.31), and Airlines dropped 20 spots to rank 88 (momentum 0.40).
* **Momentum Laggards:** Mortgage Finance (momentum 0.061, YTD rank 142) and Information Technology Services (momentum 0.079, YTD rank 141) remain deeply depressed.

## Divergences
* **Fading Leadership:** High-momentum groups are losing ground, notably Staffing & Employment Services (momentum 0.72, down 13 spots) and Integrated Freight & Logistics (momentum 0.74, down 8 spots).
* **Emerging Turnarounds:** Low-momentum commodity and utility groups are rising rapidly in rank, led by Uranium (+16 spots, momentum 0.30), Thermal Coal (+16 spots, momentum 0.41), and Drug Manufacturers - Specialty & Generic (+14 spots, momentum 0.46).
